questions.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
questions.q: The chemotherapeutic agents listed with radiotherapy in the Nigro regimen are:
questions.exp: The page states RT plus chemotherapy with 5-FU and mitomycin C. (Book p232)

questions.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
questions.q: The intended effect of the Nigro regimen before surgery is:
opts: Only symptom relief without tumour response
questions.exp: The central arrow beneath the regimen is labeled downstaging. (Book p232)

questions.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
questions.q: If complete response occurs after the Nigro regimen, the next step shown is:
questions.exp: The flowchart shows complete response leading to monitoring. (Book p232)

questions.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
questions.q: The recurrence rate after complete response mentioned in the flowchart is:
questions.exp: Beneath the monitoring branch, the page notes recurrence in about 20-30% of cases. (Book p232)

questions.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
questions.q: Recurrence after an initial complete response to the Nigro regimen is treated by:
questions.exp: The recurrence arrow in the flowchart leads to abdominoperineal resection. (Book p232)

questions.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
questions.q: Residual tumour after the Nigro regimen, when located within 5 cm, is managed by:
questions.exp: The residual-tumour branch points to APR for tumour within 5 cm. (Book p232)

units.title: Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Vascular Anatomy and Watershed Zones
units.sec: Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Vascular Anatomy and Watershed Zones · p227
units.guide: Before operations make sense, the vascular map must be clear. Griffith's point at the splenic flexure and Sudeck point at the rectosigmoid are classic watershed zones, so poor perfusion explains difficult anastomoses and segment-specific surgical caution.

units.title: Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Segmental Resections for Colonic Tumours
units.sec: Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Segmental Resections for Colonic Tumours · p227
units.guide: The colonic resection table is a practical anatomy exam: caecum means right hemicolectomy, more proximal transverse involvement pushes you toward extended right hemicolectomy, and every answer must be anchored to which bowel is removed and which vessels are tied.

units.title: Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Left-sided Colonic Resections
units.sec: Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Left-sided Colonic Resections · p228
units.guide: Left-sided colon surgery is the mirror image but not a clone. Know when to choose transverse colectomy, left hemicolectomy, or sigmoidectomy, and remember why high IMA ligation is tolerated - the rectum still receives middle and inferior rectal arterial supply.

units.title: Rectal Cancer Surgery: Landmarks and Continence-related Anatomy
units.sec: Rectal Cancer Surgery: Landmarks and Continence-related Anatomy · p228
units.guide: Low rectal surgery is governed by landmarks, not guesswork. The anorectal ring, dentate line, anal verge, and sphincters explain pain patterns as well as why a tumour within the lowest 5 cm threatens continence-preserving surgery.

units.title: Rectal Cancer Surgery: Margins, LAR versus APR and Total Mesorectal Excision
units.sec: Rectal Cancer Surgery: Margins, LAR versus APR and Total Mesorectal Excision · p229
units.guide: Rectal cancer surgery lives on margins and sphincter preservation. LAR is for higher lesions and preserves continence, APR is for very low tumours and ends with a permanent colostomy, and TME succeeds only when the holy plane is respected.

units.title: Rectal Cancer Surgery: TaTME, Complications, Nerve Injury and Obstruction
units.sec: Rectal Cancer Surgery: TaTME, Complications, Nerve Injury and Obstruction · p230
units.guide: This unit links innovation with complications. TaTME is a NOTES-based sphincter-preserving option for early tumours, but the surgeon must also anticipate leaks, abscesses, recurrence and the very specific sexual/bladder deficits produced by injury at different pelvic dissection levels.

units.title: Colorectal Cancer: Chemotherapy Regimens, Radiotherapy, Immunotherapy and Liver Metastasis
units.sec: Colorectal Cancer: Chemotherapy Regimens, Radiotherapy, Immunotherapy and Liver Metastasis · p231
units.guide: Systemic and local adjuvant therapy becomes structured here: FOLFOX versus FOLFIRI, radiotherapy for rectum not colon, and the source table's immunotherapy pairings. Finish by thinking surgically about liver metastasis - resectability depends on reserve and biology, not simply lesion count.

units.title: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen
units.sec: Anal Cancer: Prognostic Factors, Diagnosis and Nigro Regimen · p232
units.guide: The chapter ends by turning to anal cancer. Node status still dominates prognosis, CEA is for follow-up, squamous cancer carries HPV/HIV associations, and the Nigro regimen is the central treatment pathway, with APR reserved for recurrence or persistent very low disease.
